openTomorrow: Yes, I'd open it tomorrow. I just set up these notifications to keep me on track, and I'm curious to see if I can actually string together a few days without breaking the chain. Plus that daily reminder will nag me in a good way.
secured: Secured means I've verified that I completed the challenge for that day—like I did something to prove it, not just claimed I did it. That's what makes this different from other apps, I think.
freeze: I'm guessing freeze means I can pause the challenge for a day without it counting as a failure, like if something unexpected comes up and I need a break without losing my streak.
selfReported: Self-reported is when I just tell the app I did it without having to prove it with a photo or verification. Sounds less reliable but faster.
best: Setting up the notifications, honestly. It felt like I was finally taking control and committing to something. The daily reminder at a custom time felt personal—like the app was working for me, not against me.
worst: The initial awkwardness of taking that first photo as proof. Felt a bit silly at first, but I get why they do it. It's meant to keep people honest, and I respect that.
tellFriend: Yeah, I'd tell a friend. I'd say it's like a personal accountability coach in your pocket. It's simple, not preachy, and those group activity notifications remind you other people are doing the same thing. That matters.
